title: South Korea’s Arctic Container Trial Voyage Attracts Just 737 TEU, Far Below Target
content: South Korea’s first commercial container trial through the Arctic has attracted just 737 TEUs of cargo, well below the 1,300 TEUs initially targeted for the voyage, highlighting the challenge of generating sufficient demand for a new Northern Sea Route service.

title: Qatari, UAE LNG Cargoes Transferred Via Ship-to-Ship Outside Strait of Hormuz
content: Three liquefied natural gas cargoes loaded in Qatar and the United Arab Emirates have been transferred between ships outside the Strait of Hormuz in recent weeks for delivery to India and Japan, according to ship-tracking firms.

title: Port congestion on Asia sees liner schedule reliability plummet
content:
Global container shipping line reliability suffered its sharpest monthly decline in more than five years in July, as worsening congestion at major Asian ports sent on-time performance plunging.
According to Sea-Intelligence, global schedule reliability fell 6.1 percentage points month on month, to 56.4% in July – the steepest single-month decline recorded since January 2021.

title: Analysis: Time to think ‘constructively’ about Cosco
content:
Cosco Shipping Holdings has just delivered the kind of second-quarter rebound that should reassure container-shipping investors.
As disclosed at the end of last week, revenue rose 17.6% year on year to Rmb60.1bn (US$8.9bn), while profit attributable to equity holders rose 29.1% to Rmb7.5bn (US$1.1bn).
